llm.summary: This skill is a coherent AgentPMT workflow-management helper, with visible remote create, publish, delete, and restore abilities that users should handle carefully.

dimensions.detail: Remote AgentPMT calls, account setup dependencies, workflow graph data, and marketplace tool lookup are proportionate to the workflow-creation purpose and are disclosed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact contains Markdown skill documentation and a generated schema reference only; no install script, executable payload, or hidden local runtime behavior was present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions clearly describe remote AgentPMT/MCP/REST use and recommend validation before persistence, but destructive delete and restore actions do not include a separate confirmation parameter in the schema.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can mutate remote AgentPMT workflow drafts and published versions through the user's configured account, including publish, delete, and restore operations; no hidden persistence, credential harvesting, or privilege escalation was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to build and manage AgentPMT workflow skills, and the documented actions for creating, validating, updating, publishing, remixing, deleting, and restoring workflows fit that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want an agent to help manage AgentPMT workflows. Before asking it to delete, restore, publish, or attach context documents, verify the target skill ID, draft revision, and intended account because those actions can change remote workflow state through your AgentPMT setup.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The schema does expose delete, restore_published, and restore_version operations, and they can affect existing workflow work. These actions are expected for a workflow management skill and are plainly named, so this is user caution rather than evidence of malicious or suspicious behavior.
